question: Various Industrialists came together in 1944 and drafted a joint proposal for setting up a planned economy in India. It is famously known as the _________ Plan.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bombay Plan was a set of proposals for the economic development of India, put forward by eight leading industrialists in 1944.
 
• The key figures involved were J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla, Lala Shri Ram, Kasturbhai Lalbhai, Ardeshir Dalal, A.D. Shroff, and John Mathai.
 
• The plan emphasized the importance of a mixed economy with both public and private sectors playing significant roles in the economic development.
 
• It advocated for substantial government intervention in various aspects of the economy including infrastructure, healthcare, and education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bombay Plan**

 
 
• The Bombay Plan was drafted by notable Indian industrialists during the British colonial rule, aiming to outline a vision for the country's economic future post-independence.
 
• The plan proposed a significant role for the state in economic planning and development, including large-scale investments in infrastructure and social sectors.
 
• It suggested the establishment of a National Planning Commission to oversee the implementation of planned economic policies.
 
• The plan underscored the importance of achieving self-sufficiency in key industries and reducing dependence on foreign goods and technology.
 
 
 
• **Planned Economy**
 
 
• A planned economy is an economic system in which the government or central authority makes all decisions about the production and distribution of goods and services.
 
• The objective is to allocate resources efficiently to meet the needs of the population and achieve economic goals such as growth, equity, and stability.
 
• In a planned economy, the government typically controls key industries, sets prices, and determines the allocation of resources.
 
• This contrasts with a market economy, where decisions are driven by market forces such as supply and demand.
